title: Prefill Pulse Confluence: coordinated admission pacing, batch shaping, and kernel throttles to tame tail latency
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We observe tail latency spikes in mixed workloads when short low-cost streams interleave with long-prefill/high-kernel-cost requests. Current admission heuristics admit by token/time window and kernel hints independently which causes kernel thrashing and occasional CPU/GPU scheduling pressure that amplifies tails. Goal: design a coordinated admission and pacing layer (the 'Pulse Confluence') that aligns prefill admission, decode pacing, and kernel selection signals into a unified pacing decision so we can hold median latency steady while reducing 95th/99th by 25-40% for mixed workloads. Scope: admission decisioning, light-weight batch shaping (no full model changes), kernel preference scoring, and integration with existing KV cache hints and routing fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th p90 token generation latency for mixed workload benchmark reduced by >=25% vs baseline; 2) No increase in median latency >5%; 3) No regression in throughput for steady-state long-prefill jobs (>95% of baseline); 4) Feature toggles to fully disable at runtime; 5) End-to-end metrics (admit rate, held-wait-time, kernel-switch rate) emitted in Console and traced per-request.
implementation_notes:
Design summary: introduce a short-lived 'pulse' window (5-50ms tunable) during which admission uses a combined score: admission_score = w_latency*SLO_headroom + w_kernel*kernel_cost_hint + w_prefill*prefill_penalty + w_slots*available_slot_fraction. The pulse score will be evaluated per-tenant and globally with separate thresholds for dedicated vs hosted.

Admission flow changes:
- Prefill admission evaluates request token_length, decode budget, and kernel_cost_hint (from kernel profiler service).
- If pulse_score < admission_threshold, request is either: deferred into a micro-hold queue (if short) or routed to low-cost kernel variant (quantized or smaller context) where compatible.
- During decode, an adaptive pacing token-shedder will interleave small decode bursts to smooth GPU kernel handoffs and avoid attention kernel preemption.

Kernel selection integration:
- Kernel profiler emits a simple bucketed cost_hint: {low, medium, high}. Pulse weights map to cost_hint to bias admission away from high-cost kernels during pulse congestion.
- For heterogeneous racks, we add a small kernel-affinity penalty if cross-kernel context switches are likely.

Backpressure & fairness:
- Tenant-level credit buckets to avoid starvation.
- Short-request favoring when queue depth > critical_threshold to preserve tail for conversational traffic.

Implementation plan: feature-flagged rollout, start with a simulator harness within the admission service, then shadow mode in prod for one region, then gradual ramp to 50% of traffic with canary metrics and rollback on error budget triggers.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Over-eager deferral increases headroom for long jobs and could reduce throughput. Mitigation: conservative initial weights + live circuit breakers that prioritize throughput-critical routes.
Risk: Incorrect kernel cost hints cause misrouting. Mitigation: use historical cost smoothing and fall back to default kernel when unknown.
Risk: Complexity of joint score may interact with Dedicated autoscaling. Mitigation: coordinate with Dedicated autoscaler team and add a dedicated_tenant override flag.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission_score calculation, e2e simulator with synthetic mix of short/long sessions, perf benchmark on staging cluster reproducing known spike pattern. Run golden-run experiments comparing baseline vs pulse-confluence across three workloads: chat-heavy (short messages), long-prefill (large context generation), and mixed bursty traffic. Collect 50/90/95/99 quantiles, kernel-switch counts, and GPU utilization.
observability: Metrics to emit: admission_attempts, admission_deferrals, deferral_latency, kernel_switch_count, pulse_score_histogram, per-tenant_credit_balance. Traces: tag traces with pulse_decision and kernel_hint. Dashboard: new console panel under 'Serving -> Admission' showing admission loss, average hold time, and correlation to tail latency. Alerting: 95th latency spike >20% for 15m, kernel-switch-rate >2x baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit/integration tests (2 weeks). 2) Simulator validation + perf runs (1 week). 3) Shadow mode in us-west-2 for low-traffic subset (3 days) and collect metrics. 4) Canary 10% traffic for 24h; evaluate. 5) Ramp to 50% over 3 days. 6) Full enable in region if stable. Toggle to disable per-tenant and global emergency kill switch.
